_national.labelling: National wine standard GB/T 15037-2006 (originally mandatory, now a recommended standard): a vintage on the label needs at least 80% of wine from that year, a variety at least 75%, a production origin at least 80%. The revision draft keeps these definitions and lists no change to them. Wine GIs are protected as geographical indication products; four wine GIs are also protected in the EU under the 2021 EU-China agreement: Helan Mountain East Foothill, Yantai, Shacheng and Huanren Icewine.
_national.sweetness: Dry up to 4.0 g/l total sugar (or up to 9 g/l when sugar minus acidity is 2 g/l or less); semi-dry up to 12 g/l (or 18 with the acid rule); semi-sweet up to 45 g/l; sweet over 45 g/l (per the revision draft, which changes only the semi-dry definition from 2006).

cn-helan-mountain-east-foothill.labelling: Ningxia winery classification (the only official winery classification in China): introduced in 2013 with ten Fifth Growths, expanded in 2016 to five tiers from Fifth to First Growth, and re-evaluated every two years by a panel of winemakers, critics, trade and consumers; First Growths are re-examined every ten years. Classified wineries must use only grapes from their own vineyards of vines at least five years old, ferment, age and bottle on the estate, run vineyard and cellar with one team and offer visitor facilities. Status may be printed on labels. The 2021 list had 57 classified wineries (9 Second, 15 Third, 18 Fourth, 15 Fifth Growth) and no First Growth.
